t.3.18.1: Seeing his sister fallen thus, disfigured and drenched in blood, the rākṣasa Khara, burning with rage, questioned her.
t.3.18.3: Among the gods, gandharvas and beings, and the great-souled ṛṣis, who is this one of such great valour who has thus disfigured you?
t.3.18.2: You are endowed with strength and valour, you roam wherever you wish and take any form at will, and you are equal to Antaka himself. By whom have you been brought to this state, that you come here like this?
t.3.18.4: For I see no one in the world who could do me an unkindness, except the thousand-eyed great Indra, the chastiser of Pāka.
t.3.18.5: Today, with arrows that put an end to life, I shall take away their life-breaths, just as a sārasa crane drinks up the milk mingled with water.
t.3.18.6: Whose foaming red blood will the earth drink, once he has been slain by me in battle, his vital parts cut through by my arrows?
t.3.18.7: Of whom, slain by me in battle, will the birds, flocking together, tear the flesh from the body and devour it with delight?
t.3.18.8: Neither the gods nor the gandharvas, neither the piśācas nor the rākṣasas, will be able to save that wretched one, once he has been dragged down by me in the great battle.
t.3.18.9: Slowly regaining your senses, you should tell me of him, that ill-mannered one by whom you were assailed and overpowered in the forest.
t.3.18.10: Having heard these words of her brother, who was especially enraged, Śūrpaṇakhā then spoke this speech with tears.
t.3.18.12: Those two, resembling kings of the Gandharvas and endowed with the marks of royalty, whether they are gods or men, I am unable to determine.
t.3.18.11: They are two youths, endowed with beauty, delicate yet of great strength, with large eyes like white lotuses, clad in garments of bark and black antelope skin.
t.3.18.13: There, between the two of them, I saw a young woman, endowed with beauty, adorned with every ornament, and slender-waisted.
t.3.18.14: By those two, acting together on account of that young woman, I have been brought to this state, as though I were some unprotected, unchaste woman.
t.3.18.15: At the forefront of battle I wish to drink the frothing blood of that woman of crooked conduct and of those two men once they are slain.
t.3.18.16: Dear one, let this foremost desire of mine be fulfilled by you: may I drink the blood of her and of those two in battle.
t.3.18.17: As she was speaking thus, the enraged Khara commanded fourteen mighty rākṣasas, who were like Death itself.
t.3.18.18: Two men, equipped with weapons and clad in bark garments and black antelope skins, have entered the dreadful Daṇḍaka forest together with a young woman.
t.3.18.19: You should kill those two and that wicked woman, and then return. And this sister of mine will drink their blood.
t.3.18.20: O Rākṣasas, this is the cherished wish of this sister of mine: let it be fulfilled swiftly, by going and crushing those two with your own might.
t.3.18.21: Thus commanded, those fourteen rākṣasas went there together with her, like clouds driven by the wind.
